query:
Which supplied authorities help analyze the live Delhi DRC1958s14(1)(b) issue shown by this allowed record, respecting the target procedural stage, rival assertions and scope limits? Do not predict the withheld target verdict.
1. By this judgment, I will dispose off the present eviction petition filed on behalf of M/s Chandra Associates Pvt Ltd, through its Director Sh Vinod Singhal against the respondents under cite9†section 14 (1) (b) of Delhi Rent Control Act 1958, thereby praying that an order of eviction be passed in their favour and against the respondents in respect of premises no.A­15A, Hauz Khas, N. Delhi, specifically shown in red color in the site plan Evi. Ptn No.
6087/16 M/s Chandra Associates Pvt Ltd Vs Smt Krishna Gupta & Anr Page 1/15 (hereinafter referred to as the "suit shop/premises") on the ground of unauthorized and illegal occupation.
2. Brief case of the petitioner as per eviction petition is that suit premises was previously owned by Dr. Ramesh Kumar Gupta and he sold the same to petitioner vide registered sale deed and thereafter, petitioner became the absolute owner and said facts were brought to the notice of respondents by the petitioner after the purchase of the suit property.
As per petitioner, he approached respondent no.1 to handover the vacant and peaceful possession of premises but respondent failed to do so despite repeated requests and demands. As per petitioner, respondent no.1 had illegally, unauthorizedly and without the written consent of previous owner landlord Dr.
Ramesh Kumar Gupta sublet/assigned/parted with possession of premises comprising of two bedroom, drawing/dining, bathroom, English style WC, kitchen and open verandah on the front side of first floor attached to respondent no.2 and thus respondent no.2 is unauthorizedly and illegally occupying the premises. As per petitioner, respondent no.1 had no right to sublet the premises to respondent no.2 and is thus, legally liable to handover the vacant and peaceful possession of premises to the petitioner.
3. It is averred that respondent no.1 Mrs Krishna Gupta was the tenant earlier in the suit premises under Dr. Ramesh Kumar Gupta at monthly rent of Rs.1500/­ exclusive of water and electricity charges and she subsequently unauthorizedly and illegally sublet the premises to respondent no.2 in the year 1981 without the consent of previous owner landlord. As per petitioner, notice was served upon respondents to handover the vacant and peaceful possession of the suit premises but to no avail.
Hence, the present eviction petition under cite9†section 14 (1) (b) of the DRC Act against the respondents inter alia praying that eviction order be passed against the respondents in respect of suit premises i.e. A­15A, Hauz Khas, N. Delhi.
Evi. Ptn No. 6087/16 M/s Chandra Associates Pvt Ltd Vs Smt Krishna Gupta & Anr Page 2/15
4. No Written Statement was ever filed on behalf of respondent no.1 and she was proceeded exparte.
5. Written Statement was filed on behalf of respondent no.2 alleging that petition is not maintainable in view of the fact that respondent no.2 was inducted as a tenant in the suit premises by Ramesh Gupta through Smt Krishna Gupta and Tarsem Parkash Gupta but he was not being issued a proper rent receipt nor any rent agreement was executed by the parties on the pretext that Ramesh Gupta is not in India and the same will be executed on his arrival.
It is stated that Tarsem Gupta was duly authorized vide registered general power of attorney dated 26.08.1976 and on the basis of said power of attorney, respondent no.2 was inducted on 21.05.1981 as a tenant on monthly rent of Rs.1400/­ exclusive of electricity and water charges.
It is stated that respondent no.2 is occupying two bed rooms, one toilet, one drawing­cum­dining room and a kitchen on first floor of premises with complete terrace of building and a separate passage on the ground floor leading to first floor and space for car parking on ground floor.
It is stated that Ramesh Gupta visited India three­four times but written agreement could not be executed and instead of issuing proper written receipts, respondent no.1 Smt Krishna Gupta and Mr Tarsem Gupta used to issue receipts as paying guest and subsequently, respondent no.2 objected to and these objections were not acceded to, he was left with no option but to go to court of law for fixation of standard rent and for order for issuance of proper rent receipts etc.
It is further stated that when notice of petition was served upon Ramesh Gupta, Krishna Gupta and Tarsem Gupta, they came to respondent no.2 and assured that an agreement will be entered into and proper rent receipts will be issued and in pursuance thereto, a lease agreement was executed between the parties on 05.08.1983 and thereafter, Krishna Gupta and Tarsem Gupta started issuing written receipts.
Evi. Ptn No. 6087/16 M/s Chandra Associates Pvt Ltd Vs Smt Krishna Gupta & Anr Page 3/15
6. It is stated that respondent no.2 again filed a suit for fixation of standard rent as even in spite of agreement, Ramesh Gupta, Krishna Gupta and Tarsem Gupta started harassing the respondent no.2 and asked to increase the rent without any rhyme or reason.
It is further averred that in the second petition filed under cite10†section 6 & cite11†9 of the DRC Act, respondents therein filed written statement and they accepted the execution of lease deed dated 05.08.1983 between parties, which confirms that respondent Arun Chopra is legal tenant of Ramesh Gupta through Krishna Gupta and Tarsem Gupta and as such, petition is liable to be rejected on this ground.
7. As per respondent no.2, a notice was issued by Income Tax Department qua fraudulent deal between Ramesh Gupta and M/s Chandra Associates, which fact was covered in newspaper Statesman dated 10.05.1987 and endorsement was to respondent no.2 herein. It is stated that respondent no.2 submitted his reply on 22.05.1989 to said notice.
It is stated that Krishna Gupta and Tarsem Gupta also submitted their statement in pursuance of aforesaid notice wherein they have admitted that the respondent no.2 is tenant of Sh Ramesh Gupta through them in the aforesaid premises. It is claimed that respondent no.2 was and is a tenant in premises in question since 1981. It is alleged that there is no cause of action for petitioner to file present petition.
8. As per respondent, M/s Chandra Associates has no interest in property and are not the owner of property, however it is admitted that M/s Chandra Associates have written a letter to respondent no.2 that they have purchased the property from Ramesh Gupta and at present they are the owner and respondent no.2 should pay damages but they have failed to produce any title document.
It is stated that tenancy of respondent no.2 was never terminated and as such, he is a legal tenant in suit property and Chandra Associates have no legal right to ask the respondent no.2 to vacate Evi. Ptn No. 6087/16 M/s Chandra Associates Pvt Ltd Vs Smt Krishna Gupta & Anr Page 4/15 the premises on any ground. It is alleged that petitioner is unauthorized occupant and a tresspasser in the property and as such, has no locus standi to file present petition.
It is alleged that site plan as supplied, is not depicting the correct position as per site and lease deed.
9. It is denied that M/s Chandra Associates are the landlord of suit property. It is further denied that name and address of tenant is Krishan Gupta, 446, Sainik Farm, New Delhi. It is alleged that Krishna Gupta was never a tenant in property rather she alongwith her husband who was power of attorney holder of said property, were / are the representatives of Ramesh Gupta.
It is further denied that respondent no.1 unauthorizedly and without consent of previous landlord, Ramesh Gupta sublet the premises to respondent no.2. It is claimed that respondent no.2 is occupying the premises as a tenant with due knowledge and consent of Ramesh Gupta and rent is being taken by Smt Krishna Gupta or Tarsem Gupta on behalf of Ramesh Gupta which fact has already been admitted in Inquiry Report filed before Income Tax Officer.
It is alleged that when respondent no.2 was out of station, the so called landlord also created unauthorized construction in the premises. It is further denied that premises were let out to respondent no.1 by Dr Ramesh Gupta and thereafter and respondent no.1 sublet it to respondent no.2 on monthly rent of Rs.1500/­ exclusive of water and electricity charges.
It is stated that Ramesh Gupta while going abroad had given the keys of whole premises no.A­15A, Hauz Khas to his brother Tarsem Gupta and his sister­in­law Smt Krishna Gupta duly authorizing them with GPA. It is alleged that petitioner has suppressed material facts.
10. It is further denied that premises in occupation were sold to petitioner by previous owner Ramesh Gupta. It is alleged that transaction of property was also questioned as being illegal and Income Tax Department was interested to occupy the premises as certain dues were to be cleared to Evi. Ptn No. 6087/16 M/s Chandra Associates Pvt Ltd Vs Smt Krishna Gupta & Anr Page 5/15 Income Tax Department and the deal between Ramesh Gupta and petitioner attracted FERA violations.
It is reiterated that premises were let out to respondent no.2 by respondent no.1 and Tarsem Gupta under authority/instructions of Ramesh Gupta. It is alleged that petitioner raised unauthorized and illegal construction over the property and encroached upon terrace portion in possession of respondent no.2. It is alleged that the contents of petition are totally false and frivolous. All other averments are denied. It is prayed that the present petition may be dismissed.
11. Replication was filed by the petitioner to the WS of respondent no.2, denying the objections raised by respondent no.2. It is alleged that averments raised by respondent no.2 are malafide, concocted and baseless. Averments of petition were reiterated.
12. It is stated that Tarsem Gupta is stranger to present case. It is denied that Tarsem Gupta had any right to induct respondent no.2 as tenant in premises. It is stated that if at all, there is any power of attorney in favour of said Tarsem Gupta, the same is nothing but a forged document. It is admitted that rent receipts were issued by respondent no.1 who inducted the respondent no.2 into the premises unauthorizedly and illegally and without written consent of earlier owner of property.
It is stated that neither Ramesh Gupta nor petitioner executed any agreement with respondent no.2 and any other agreement executed with respondent no.2 by any other person has no legal value. It is further denied that Ramesh Gupta started harassing the respondent no.2. It is further denied that Ramesh Gupta accepted the respondent as tenant in his written statement rather respondent no.1 accepted respondent no.2 as tenant.
It is further denied that there was any fraudulent deal with Sh Ramesh Gupta and petitioner. It is stated that notice from Income Tax Department has nothing to do with present case and secondly, if any false statement is made by respondent no.2 before any Evi. Ptn No. 6087/16 M/s Chandra Associates Pvt Ltd Vs Smt Krishna Gupta & Anr Page 6/15 authority same does not bind petitioner to accept the same. It is further denied that petitioner has no interest in property or is not owners of same.
It is further denied that petitioner is unauthorized occupant and tresspasser. It is further denied that respondent no.2 is in occupation of two bed room, one toilet, one drawing and dining room with a kitchen on first floor with complete terrace of building and a separate passage on the ground floor leading to first floor and space for car parking on the ground floor. It is reiterated that respondent no.2 is illegal and unauthorized occupant of premises.
It is further denied that respondent no.2 has been occupying the premises since May 1981 as tenant of Ramesh Gupta. It is further denied that Ramesh Gupta executed any power of attorney in favour of Smt Krishna Gupta and Sh Tarsem Gupta on any alleged date. It is stated that said document is forged. It is stated that rent taken by Smt Krishna Gupta or Tarsem Gupta is illegal.
It is stated that Ramesh Gupta never inducted or accepted respondent no.2 as tenant in the said property and in fact, respondent no.1 who was a tenant of Ramesh Gupta, illegally and unauthorizedly inducted respondent no.2 as tenant without the written consent of Ramesh Gupta. It is further denied that site plan filed is not correct. It is further denied that petitioner carried out any unauthorized construction in the premises.
It is stated that petitioner being the rightful owner of property has every right to carry out the construction in the above property. It is further denied that Ramesh Gupta while going abroad gave keys of his premises to his brother and sister­in­law with alleged power of attorney. It is further denied that petitioner unauthorizedly locked the main gate of premises. All other objections have been denied and the averments of the petition has been reiterated.
13. Thereafter, evidence by way of affidavit of Vinod Singhal, Director of Chandra Associates was filed on 25.09.2002 and documents were even Evi. Ptn No. 6087/16 M/s Chandra Associates Pvt Ltd Vs Smt Krishna Gupta & Anr Page 7/15 exhibited as per the affidavit. Following documents were exhibited vide said affidavit:­
a) copy of sale deed as registered document no.6883 and no.6884 in additional book no.1, volume no.5576, page 36­42 dated 11/12.08.1986 as Mark A and Mark A1
b) site plan as Ex.P1
c) receipts dated 08.03.1986 and 23.11.1983 as Mark C & Mark B
d) carbon copy of notice to provide documents dated 09.02.1999 as Ex.P2 and reply thereto as Ex.P3
e) photocopy of power of attorney dated 26.05.1976 executed by Dr Ramesh Gupta as Mark D and copy of agreement dated 05.08.1983 between respondent no.1 & 2 as Mark E.
f) certified copy of petition no. SR­36/85 filed by Arun Chopra against Smt Krishna Gupta and other for fixation of standard rent alongwith memo of parties as Ex.P5 and certified copy of WS dated 11.02.1986 by respondent no.1 & 2 as Ex.P6.
g) certified copy of WS dated 10.09.1995 by respondent no.3 to amended petition in above case as Ex.P7
h) certificate copy of order dated 04.03.1995 of Ld ARC disposing of two applications, one under Order I Rule 10 CPC and another under Order 22 Rule 10 CPC on behalf of Chandra Associates as Ex.P8
i) copy of WS dated July 1986 filed by Dr Ramesh Kumar Gupta already Ex.P5
j) Form no.32 of cite12†Companies Act dated 08.09.1987 as Mark F and copy of resolution of Company dated 09.11.1990 as Mark G
k) Form no.32 of Companies Act dated 08.09.1987 as Mark H and Form no.32 of the Companies Act dated 25.09.1987 as Mark I and Form no.32 of the Companies Act dated 08.09.1987 as Mark J.
14. Thereafter, petitioner examined summoned witness Mr Surender Kumar, LDC, Sub Registrar­III, Asaf Ali Road as PW2 who brought the original sale deed (earlier Mark A) and exhibited the same as Ex.PW2/1. He also brought sale deed (earlier Mark A­1) and exhibited the same as Ex.PW2/2. This witness was duly cross examined.
15. Thereafter, petitioner examined summoned witness Mr L S Dhik, Evi. Ptn No. 6087/16 M/s Chandra Associates Pvt Ltd Vs Smt Krishna Gupta & Anr Page 8/15 JTA, Registrar of Companies, Lodhi Road as PW3 (wrongly mentioned as AW3) who brought the summoned record. He deposed that as per records, Chandra Associates Pvt Ltd was incorporated on 26.05.1986. Photocopy thereof is Mark X.
He further deposed that in 1986, as per their record, there were two Directors in the petitioner company namely Mrs Manju Rani Mital and Mr Mahender Kumar. He further deposed that Vinod Singhal was appointed as Director w.e.f. 01.09.1989.
16. Thereafter, Mr. Manoj Singhal, Director M/s Chandra Associates Pvt Ltd was examined as PW1. He tendered his evidence by way of affidavit Ex.PW1/A and relied upon following documents :­
a) sale deed dated 11/12 August 1986 already Ex.PW2/2,
b) site plan as Ex.PW1/1,
c) copy of legal notice dated 09.02.1999 already Ex.P2,
d) reply to the said legal notice dated 16.02.1999 already Ex.P3,
e) certified copy of the earlier petition filed by respondent no.2 alongwith memo of parties already Ex.P6,
f) certified copy of WS already Ex.P7,
g) certified copy of amended WS already Ex.P8,
h) certified copy of order dated 04.03.1995 already Ex.P9,
i) certified copy of WS of respondent no.3 Ramesh Kumar as Ex.PW1/10,
j) resolution dated 09.11.1990 as Ex.PW1/12,
k) Form No. 32 of the cite12†Companies Act dated 10.08.1987, dated 18.08.1987, dated 20.08.1987 and 01.09.1989 as Ex. PW1/11, Ex.PW1/13, Ex.PW1/14 & Ex.PW1/15 (all OSR),
l) certified copy of resolution dated 06.07.2008 as Ex.PW1/16.
17. This witness was cross examined by counsel for respondent no.2.
During his cross­examination, he admitted the document Mark D & Mark E Evi. Ptn No. 6087/16 M/s Chandra Associates Pvt Ltd Vs Smt Krishna Gupta & Anr Page 9/15 which is mentioned in para 5 of his affidavit. Thereafter, PE was closed on 23.09.2017 and respondent no.2 was given opportunity to lead evidence.
18. Respondent no.2 examined summoned witness Mr Rajinder Singh, Record Attendant, Department of Archives as R2W2 who brought the summoned record i.e. sale deed dated 31.10.1967 executed by Mr Krishnamachari K V in favour of Ramesh Kumar Gupta. Certified copy thereof is Ex.R2W2/1. He has also brought the record of sale deed dated 29.01.1987 executed by Ved Prakash Gupta HUF in favour of Vinod Singhal. Certified copy thereof is Ex.R2W2/2.
He has also brought GPA dated 26.08.1976 executed by Dr Ramesh Kumar Gupta in favour of Tarsem Prakash. Copy of same is Ex.R2W2/3. Witness was cross examined and discharged.
19. Thereafter, respondent no.2 examined summoned witness Mr L Baxla, Judicial Assistant, Ahlmad posted in the court of Dr Ajay Gulati, Ld. ADJ­02, South, Saket Courts who brought case file PC No.5917/2016 titled as cite13†Pawan Kumar Gupta Vs State Ors and exhibited the order dated 18.11.2015 as Ex.R2W3/A (OSR). He has also exhibited the above Probate Petition consisting of 1 to 20 pages as Ex.R2W3/B (OSR) (colly). Witness was cross examined and discharged.
20. Thereafter, respondent no.2 examined summoned witness Mr Naresh Kaushik, Judicial Assistant, Record Room Criminal, South, Saket Courts who brought case file bearing FIR No.664/1999, PS Hauz Khas, u/s 342/147/149 cite14†IPC titled as cite15†State vs Manoj Kumar . He compared the certified copy of chargesheet and report under cite16†section 173 Cr.P.C. of SHO Hauz Khas dated 23.01.2001 with file and exhibited the same as Ex.R2W4/A (colly) (OSR).
He also compared the certified copies of statement of Sandeep Kumar, S/o Shiv Kumar, statement of Manoj Kumar, S/o Shiv Kumar, statement of Jai Mal Singhal, W/o Sh. Shiv Kumar, statement of Evi. Ptn No. 6087/16 M/s Chandra Associates Pvt Ltd Vs Smt Krishna Gupta & Anr Page 10/15 Poonam Singhal, W/o Sandeep Kumar, statement of Gopal Bansal, S/o Jwala Prasad, statement of Ashish Chankun, APP, statement of Captain Arun Chopra, S/o late Sh.
Amolak Ram Chopra, statement of all accused persons, all dated 25.04.2011, which are found to be same. Same are Ex.R2W4/B (colly) (OSR). This witness was cross examined and discharged.
21. Evidence affidavit of respondent no.2 Arun Chopra was filed on 25.10.2017, however he never tendered his evidence. On 15.02.2019, the counsel for respondent no.2 stated that respondent evidence may be closed. Same was closed accordingly.
